Done — passed on the first execution.

**Approach** (`out/T1/solution.py`): stream the 244 source tensors with `safe_open`, drop anything matching `gpt_neox.layers.(2|6|10|14).`, and write survivors into a *fresh* dict under their remapped name (`old -> new` from the ordered list of kept indices). Building a new dict rather than renaming in place removes the collision hazard entirely; an explicit `new_key in tensors` check would fire if a remap were ever wrong.

**Checks enforced** (all fail with non-zero exit before any write): no `layers.12/13/14/15.` keys remain, exactly 12 `attention.query_key_value.weight` tensors, indices contiguous 0..11, exactly 184 output tensors, and each surviving block still owns all 15 of its tensors.

Output: `out/T1/model.safetensors`, 184 tensors, 1.67 GB. Self-report in `out/T1/REPORT.md`.
